records.element: Script — all 11 lines (v3)
records.choice: The v3 script (files/short-eo03-first-message-script-v3.md): v2 verbatim except L6 — 'And they came — children, hunters, strangers the maker never met — and to each of them the hand still speaks: I was here.' (DR-E3G-L6 in that doc).
records.alternatives: v2's L6 (two colons in one breath at the emotional peak) — superseded; deeper L6 cuts — rejected, the measured runtime (~62 s) never broke the ceiling that made L6 the designated cut.
records.context: Hadi scored the v2 transcript 80–85 (2026-10-24) and ordered improvement; the change removes the colon pile-up and binds the still/still/still-speaking spine across L2/L6/L10.
records.why: One surgical change, earned; every other line was audited and deliberately left — manufacturing more edits would be randomness, not improvement.
records.change: A canon ruling or a retention signal against a specific line reopens that line's block in the script doc.

records.element: Scene plate — the maker blowing pigment (L1 + opening card)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: blank-oval maker in a rust tunic presses a hand to ROUGH cave rock and blows red-ochre dust from a hollow bone; the torch stands fully inside the frame; the upper rock is dark and empty. Inspected by eye (V-06).
records.alternatives: The v3 flat-cartoon plate — the 30-scored visual's opening frame, its title colliding with the figure's head; rejected wholesale by the exemplar rebuild.
records.context: EP3-GAPS findings F2/F6/F7; format v4 world anchors (oval head, rust tunic) kept — the failure was thinness, not the grammar.
records.why: The first line is a process; the plate performs it in a textured, lit world instead of a pictogram.
records.change: If Studio retention dips at 0–5 s, the opening image is the first suspect.

records.element: Scene plate — the cave wall (L2, L5, L7, L9, L10 state 3, L11 base)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: a solid rock FACE seen straight on — irregular stone, cracks, one smoother dark panel at centre for the hand element, torch glow only along the bottom edge. Second generation; the first (a tunnel-like alcove in boulders) was rejected at inspection and the rejection is in the job file.
records.alternatives: v3's coursed stone-block wall (read as masonry, torches clipped at both edges) — the F5 defect; the first v4 generation (tunnel) — rejected on sight.
records.context: QC H-01: the wall is the canvas; the alcove panel is the planned negative space the hand element occupies.
records.why: A cave wall that reads as a cave wall; the message's home for four lines plus the close.
records.change: If phone checks show the lower word band fighting the rock texture, the bands rise into the panel's dark flanks, never over the hand.

records.element: Element — the hand stencil (separate component)
records.choice: NEW element: a TRUE NEGATIVE stencil — pale hand silhouette inside a red-ochre spray halo, generated on pure black; screen blend drops the black so the pale hand and its pigment halo sit on the wall plate. 680×680 centred on the wall's smooth panel. Fades in over L2's first 0.9 s, yields to the photograph at 'still there today,' returns for L5/L7/L9, the bookend's third state and the bridge.
records.alternatives: v3's flat RED POSITIVE silhouette (a handprint icon — real stencils are negative; BF1 disclosed the defect and shipped it) — fixed here at the element level; a CSS-drawn hand (banned, V-13).
records.context: H-01 separate components; the stencil is the episode's hero and its one concrete example (T-17); EP3-GAPS finding F4 (the hero was three different objects in v3 — now one element, one identity, everywhere).
records.why: One element carries the whole arc — maker (L1's act) → survivor (L2) → waiter (L5) → statement (L7) → proof (L9) → voice (L10).
records.change: A viewer misreading the blend as glow reopens the blend/opacity choice.

records.element: Scene plate — the carriers (L3; sinking through L4; bookend state 2)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: a grey-bunned elder — blank oval, series grammar — telling the story to four huddled oval listeners around a small fire, deep cave above for the word bands. Second generation; the first gave the elder a fully faced, realistic head among the ovals (generator drift, no register justification) and was rejected at inspection.
records.alternatives: The first v4 generation (faced elder) — rejected: Ep.4's faced grandmother was a DELIBERATE register shift for a viewer-world beat, logged and flagged for Hadi; an accidental face here would be an unowned inconsistency.
records.context: N-06: the villain (the dying witness) needs the carriers present before they are lost; format v4 world anchors.
records.why: The carriers are people the viewer can read at a glance, in a cave with depth — the 'before' the wall replaces.
records.change: Hadi's pending register verdict on Ep.4's faced grandmother, if it goes the other way, reopens this plate's elder too.

records.element: Scene plate — the dead fire (L4, second state)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: charred logs, a few embers, one thread of smoke in near-darkness. Cut in mid-L4 at the first word of 'the message dies too' (timestamp computed from the alignment, never hand-typed), after the carriers plate has sunk to 45% brightness across the line's first half.
records.alternatives: v3's single device (dimming the carriers to 0.55 and holding) — kept and strengthened: the dim now ENDS in a cut to the dead fire itself; the death is shown, not just darkened.
records.context: S-08: state changes must construct meaning; N-06's villain lands here.
records.why: When the last rememberer dies, the fire is out — the viewer watches the light leave and then sees what is left.
records.change: If frame QC finds the cut reading as a glitch, the cut becomes a 0.3 s crossfade in the extras layer.

records.element: Scene plate — the visitors (L6)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: a child, a spear-carrying hunter and a grey-bearded elder seen from behind, before the stencil at TRUE scale on the wall, torch in its bracket fully inside the frame. The stencil here is painted into the plate — the same negative form as the element (pale hand, ochre halo), so the hero's identity holds across the cut.
records.alternatives: v3's visitors plate (a giant glowing palm ≈4× human scale floating over a cave mouth) — the F4 scale defect; reusing the carriers plate — rejected in v3 and still right: these are people the maker never met. A THIRD generation with the figures in the bottom third (wide empty wall for the words) was tried during the v4 QC cycle and REJECTED: it solved the word band but drifted flat and posterized against the episode's painterly plates — archived in the build folder's rejected/ with the reason (pride-rule fix P8's sibling). The original plate stands; the band moved instead (DR-E3G-WORD-2).
records.context: L6's job: prove the message speaks to strangers; backs to the viewer = the viewer stands with them.
records.why: The strangers receive the message at its real size, in a real place — the claim stays honest at the moment it is proven.

records.element: Component — the real Pettakere photograph (L2, 'still there today')
records.choice: The genuine hand-stencil photograph from Pettakere Cave, Sulawesi (CC BY-SA 4.0, Cahyo, Wikimedia Commons; minimum age 39,900 years per the Commons record — the episode's own 'forty thousand years'), pre-cropped to 9:16 and shown FULL-BLEED from the first word of 'It is still there today' to the line's end (~1.5 s), the generated hand fading out beneath it. Its attribution rides in a caption strip INSIDE the component. The spoken words and the bug render ABOVE the photograph (a layer repair in the scene's extras: the first v4 render's frame check caught the photo covering both for its whole window — pride-rule fix P9). Publish obligation unchanged: the CC BY-SA attribution also goes in the YouTube description.
records.alternatives: BF1's glass-plate inset (~15% of frame area, ~1.2 s) — said=shown on paper, experienced as a footnote (finding F3); keeping the generated hand for the whole line — rejected: at the proof sentence, only the real thing is proof.
records.context: SAID = SHOWN at full size; audit A-10's fix, promoted from inset to the beat itself; intro-v4 glass grammar NOT used — this is Earth One, and the photograph needs no frame to be believed.
records.why: The episode claims a mark survived 40,000 years; at the exact words, the viewer stops looking at a drawing of the claim and looks at the claim.
records.change: If the photo's softness at full-bleed reads as a defect on phone checks, the fall-back is the same photograph at 85% frame over the dimmed wall — never back to the postage stamp.

records.element: Scene plate — the dawnland (L8)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: a vast pale dawn — huge peach sky, a distant cliff line, ONE tiny cave mouth with a faint red glint, empty golden plain. Through L8 the plate PULLS BACK (scale 1.13 → 1.00, overriding the engine's push-in): the world gets bigger and the cave gets smaller while the words stay pinned at centre frame.
records.alternatives: v3 staged L8 on the visitors plate (the comers, again) — the distance the line is about was never shown; a push-in (the engine default) — the exact opposite of the line's meaning.
records.context: Word Choreography Doctrine: visuals do narrative work; 'It cannot travel' is performed by the only camera move in the piece that retreats.
records.why: Whoever wants the message must cross all of this — the frame makes the viewer feel the crossing.
records.change: If the pull-back reads as a rendering error in QC frames, its range narrows (1.09 → 1.00) before any other change.

records.element: Scene plate — the savanna (L10, state 1 only)
records.choice: NEW painterly plate: a rich dawn savanna — textured grass, a spotted deer herd, one acacia, pink-gold sky — Ep.1's world redrawn at the new standard. Used ONLY for the bookend's first state ('the first archive was a body'), with dark-ink words and a dark-ink bug.
records.alternatives: v3's borrowed Observations finale plate carrying L10 + L11 + the end card (~16 s of near-empty pale field — finding F1, the close abandoning the episode) — retired from this piece; the bookend is now three states in three worlds.
records.context: N-08 bookend: the archives arrive in THEIR OWN worlds in turn — body (savanna), story (the carriers' fire), mark (the wall) — cut on the spoken names.
records.why: The recap is a journey through the series, not a caption over an empty field.
records.change: If Ep.1's own v4 rebuild redraws its savanna, this plate follows that build's world.

records.element: Component — the speaking glow (L6)
records.choice: A soft radial torchlight glow (screen blend) centred on the visitors plate's stencil, opacity swelling on a sine curve across 'the hand still speaks: I was here' — computed from the aligned start of 'speaks:' — and gone by the line's end.
records.alternatives: A static glow for the whole line (decoration, not an event); animating the plate itself (the plate is a photograph-like painting — moving it breaks its reality).
records.context: Word Choreography Doctrine applied to an element: the mark LIGHTS as it speaks — the episode's central impossibility, performed.
records.why: At the proof line, the hero answers — visibly.
records.change: If the swell reads as a lens artifact in QC, its peak opacity drops (0.8 → 0.5) before its timing moves.

records.element: Word placement — blow + wall lines (L1, L2, L5, L7, L9, L11)
records.choice: Cream words, amber key, text shadow. Blow: bands y 470/590 on the dark rock above the maker. Wall lines: bands y 1310/1415, BELOW the hand element, on the wall's darker lower rock.
records.alternatives: Words above the hand — rejected as in v3: the hero keeps its space (Q-c, S-05 one focal element).
records.context: V-16 + V-14 safe rect (the layout plan audits itself: 0 violations); placement follows each scene's own negative space.
records.why: The eye's path is hand (the claim) → words (the sentence), never the two in competition.
records.change: Per-frame QC verdicts govern.

records.element: Word placement — carriers, visitors, embers (L3, L4, L6)
records.choice: Cream/amber with shadow. Carriers + embers: bands y 615/725 in the dark cave above the fire. Visitors: bands y 865/935 — placed by MEASUREMENT between the stencil's bottom (y≈810) and the hunter's crown (y≈990), ~15 px clear of both (v3 used 1000/1110; the first v4 render at 950/1060 still put 'I was here.' on the hunter's crown — frame-verified, pride-rule fixes P2 + P10). Known compromise, recorded: the hunter's thin dark spear shaft crosses behind the widest phrases' first word; it is 14 px of dark wood on dark rock and the cream glyphs stay legible over it — the alternative (a regenerated lower-figures plate) was rejected for style drift (DR-E3G-IMG-6).
records.alternatives: One band set for the whole episode — the subtitle habit returning; rejected in every prior episode and here.
records.context: V-16 placement is per-scene, planned at image time; both plates were generated and inspected with their word space identified.
records.why: Words never touch a face, a flame, a spear, or the hand.
records.change: Per-frame QC verdicts govern.

records.element: Word placement — the pale scenes (L8 dawnland, L10 state 1 savanna)
records.choice: Dark-brown words, rust key, NO shadow — the Ep.2 pale-sky grammar. Dawnland bands y 615/725 in the open sky; savanna bands y 470/590 in the dawn sky above the deer.
records.alternatives: Cream words — invisible on these skies; the measured Ep.2 lesson, and the same failure the cream bug commits on pale scenes (DR-E3G-CARD-3).
records.context: V-16: contrast is the readability rule; placement follows the scene.
records.why: The words join each scene's own light instead of importing the cave's.

records.element: Word placement — the bookend's three states (L10)
records.choice: Per-PHRASE scenes in the layout plan: phrases through 'body.' are savanna (dark ink, sky bands), phrases through 'story.' are carriers (cream, cave bands), the rest are wall (cream, below-hand bands). The two v3 finale typography labels are DROPPED — picture, words and voice now carry the recap; a label would be a third signal saying the same thing (pride-rule fix P3).
records.alternatives: One scene + labels for the whole line (v3) — the typography-on-emptiness close that scored 30.
records.context: N-08 bookend with a twist; S-05 one signal at a time; the layout fork implements the per-phrase scene split and the builder cuts plates on the aligned word starts.
records.why: Each archive is NAMED in its own world at the moment it is spoken — the recap is the series in miniature.
records.change: If a state cut lands mid-phrase in QC, the cut timestamps move to the phrase boundary, not the word.

records.element: Word timing + chunking (all scenes)
records.choice: faster-whisper word timestamps mapped to the script's exact words: 160 display words mapped, 3 line-window boundary starts clamped by the layout (the pipeline's designed handling). Phrases of ≤3 words appear cumulatively and clear before the next phrase; key words are the accent set, amber at +18% with an overshoot pop. One latent defect fixed: v3's accent set named 'speaks' but the display word is 'speaks:' — the accent never fired in v3; the fork's set names the true display word.
records.alternatives: Whole-line captions (banned); per-word karaoke over a full line (reads as a subtitle).
records.context: Format v4 word-animation spec. COUNT NOTE: v2's script doc claimed 159 words and v3's build repeated it; the aligned map of the same text counts 160 display words — the claim did not survive recount (the same failure EP1-GAPS found in Ep.1's '162'). This build's ground truth is words.json: 160.
records.why: At most 3 words exist at any instant, each arriving with its spoken moment — and the count is measured, not inherited.
records.change: Whisper boundary error >~150 ms on a re-alignment reopens the mapping.

records.element: Word choreography — 25 words with decided motion
records.choice: Per-word animation decisions, implemented as behaviour tags in the engine and listed with their reasons in the script doc (files/short-eo03-first-message-script-v3.md §Word choreography) and per word in this file's word_decisions data. Headlines: L3's three carriers SETTLE smaller as they are handed on; L4's death-words SINK and 'remembers' FADES; L6's 'speaks:' FLIPS to face the viewer and 'here.' GROWS to the piece's largest word; L8's 'travel.' is TETHERED — strains right, pulled back; 'still' (L2) grows and holds, binding the spine.
records.alternatives: Uniform appearance for all words (the 'appear and disappear' captioning Hadi named as the failure); choreographing EVERY word (motion everywhere is noise — the doctrine is decided behaviour, and stillness is a decision where it serves the beat).
records.context: Word Choreography Doctrine (Hadi, 2026-10-24): an undecided word behaviour is randomness; a decided one guides the eye to the objective.
records.why: The words perform the story's verbs: staying, dying, waiting, speaking, refusing to travel, refusing to forget.
records.change: Hadi's re-score: any choreographed word that reads as gimmick at phone size loses its tag to a recorded as-is, in this record.

records.element: Word Decision Container — coverage gate
records.choice: EVERY word in the piece carries a recorded decision in this file's word_decisions array: its treatment (a choreography tag, the accent pop, or a deliberate AS-IS), its measured tempo, and its reason (story function / tempo / why this treatment or why none). The builder ASSERTS coverage — a word without a record fails the build. Coverage at build: 160 of 160.
records.alternatives: Recording only the special words (the pre-doctrine pattern: 25 decided, 135 silent defaults — defaults are exactly what the doctrine names as randomness).
records.context: Word Decision Container doctrine (Hadi, 2026-10-24 ~17:47 ET): 'Don't leave it to randomness' — coverage is countable and gates the piece.
records.why: The exemplar is the pattern other pieces replicate; its word layer must be auditable word by word.
records.change: The reasons are generated per word from its tempo, its phrase's decided event, and its grammatical role — if Hadi wants richer per-word prose, the container's schema already holds it.

records.element: Music + narration track
records.choice: The v3 audio chain, unchanged in method: guide-voice lines normalised per line (A-11), the LOW synth-pad cave bed ducked ≈13 dB, stereo pan before mastering, master chain without dynaudnorm (standing law). ONE line re-voiced: L6, same TTS voice (avocado_v2:MAI_03), for the v3 script's new wording; all other lines keep their v3 takes. Music-only twin rebuilt alongside for the clone swap.
records.alternatives: Re-voicing all lines for consistency — rejected: the other takes are the approved performances; re-rolling them risks regression for no gain. A composed melody — rejected in v3 (Q-e) and still.
records.context: QC A-section; A-07: the delivered file is re-measured independently in QC (this build: see the job file's Verify section).
records.why: The bed is the cave's hush under the voice, never a rival to it.
records.change: The cloned-voice pass swaps narration via the music-only twin, per the standing ladder.

records.element: Packaging — title
records.choice: "The Message That Outlived Its Maker" — unchanged from v2/v3 (the 'First' surrender on the Blombos/Diepkloof record stands).
records.alternatives: Keeping 'First' for click strength — rejected on truth in v2; nothing in this round reopens it.
records.context: S-09; the title is a paradox the piece resolves.
records.why: The click is bought with a gap, not with a claim a comment can kill.
records.change: CTR data after publish is the comparison baseline.

records.element: Packaging — cover
records.choice: BUILT AT LAST: DR-E3-CLICK's designated cover — the real Pettakere photograph full-bleed 9:16 with the cover line 'STILL THERE TODAY.' — checked legible at 180 px. (v3 shipped the opening-card frame as its cover and never built this one — finding F2.)
records.alternatives: The opening-card frame (v3's substitution — a title card, not the proof object); the visitors plate (strong, but a drawing of the claim where the photograph IS the claim).
records.context: S-09 designated cover frame; DR-E3-CLICK named this frame and this line in the script doc before v3 was built.
records.why: In the feed, the survivor itself makes the promise: a real hand, still there today.
records.change: The 180 px verdict in QC is the last word; the visitors frame is the named fallback.

records.element: Container — opening card (1.6 s)
records.choice: Blow plate + EARTH ONE + the episode title in amber, text block placed by MEASUREMENT on the plate's clear dark rock: the maker's head-top measures y≈829 on the displayed plate, so the block runs EARTH ONE y 380, title y 560/672 — the whole block clears the dome by ~65 px, with the radial scrim (recentered to 30%) as insurance. History: the first v4 placement (y 600/770/880) still clipped the dome's left shoulder in the first render's frame check — the same defect class as v3's card (F2) — and was re-placed from the pixel measurement, not by eye (pride-rule fixes P1 + P8).
records.alternatives: Cold-open on narration (a format-level question held open series-wide, not adopted per episode).
records.context: Earth One format v4 container; cards are titles, not subtitles.
records.why: The card names channel and episode before the hook, legibly, without sitting on the maker's head.
records.change: The open container-vs-hook question, when Hadi settles it, applies here first.

records.element: Container — end card (3.4 s)
records.choice: The WALL plate (the episode's own world) + 'FOLLOW FOR THE REST OF THE STORY' + NEXT tease naming Ep.4 ('A SONG REMEMBERS WHAT WORDS FORGET') + EARTH ONE, in the cave's cream/amber grammar (colours re-grammared from v3's rust-on-pale — pride-rule fix P5).
records.alternatives: v3's end card over the borrowed pale finale — retired with finding F1: the piece ends in its own world now, on the wall where its message still is.
records.context: Format v4 close: spoken bridge (L11) + FOLLOW end card; the ask is made three ways (bridge, card, description) because N-09 forbids hiding it in metaphor.
records.why: The last frame is the hero's home, not a borrowed dawn.

records.element: Container — EARTH ONE bug (per-scene ink: the Action #32 proposal)
records.choice: Small bold 'EARTH ONE' at top-left (x=100, y=265) during content, ink matched per scene: cream at 69% on the dark cave scenes, DARK BROWN at 78% on the two pale scenes (L8 dawnland; L10's savanna state) — one colour value per scene in CONFIG (bugByLine + the bookend's state override). This is the built proposal for Action #32, judged by Hadi in the piece at re-score; reversing it is a one-value swap.
records.alternatives: Fixed cream everywhere (v3: illegible for the piece's entire pale final quarter — the defect #32 exists to settle); no bug (attribution lost). Ep.4 already ships scene-matched ink; this extends the same answer to Ep.3, where the pale stretch is one scene and one state, not a quarter of the piece.
records.context: Format v4 container; V-14 safe rect; Hadi's standing rule that proposals attached to scored pieces are judged as built artifacts.
records.why: A bug that cannot be read is not a bug; per-scene ink keeps attribution's job done in both palettes.
records.change: Hadi's #32 verdict at re-score settles it series-wide; if he rules cream-everywhere, the two pale values swap back and the dawnland's legibility cost is his to accept knowingly.

accepted_exceptions_note: No accepted exception is on record for this piece. (Format rule carried from migration-2: acceptances are revisable and would ride here with a status_note; none exist to carry.)
